messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Surge: /v1/chat/completions has sustained high RPS and auth failures. Possible credential stuffing + scrapers. Paging SRE.

Alice (oncall): on it — standing up monitoring. Any IP patterns or UA fingerprints yet?

Ben SRE: early signal: many requests from 45.77.96.0/22 and 103.21.50.0/24. UA strings vary but lots of `python-requests` + empty referer. Failed auth spikes from same ranges.

Carla PM: are customers seeing errors? We got a support note about 429s and slow responses from a partner.

Sasha Support: yes — two customers reported throttling and timeouts ~12:07 UTC. Filed tickets and asked for urgency.

Gaurav-Sec: quick proposal: 1) temporary WAF ACL to block offending CIDRs 2) enable per-key adaptive throttling for suspicious signatures 3) force exponential backoff headers for repeat offenders. Also recommend rotating any tokens with abnormal auth patterns.

Alice (oncall): agree. Ben, can you push WAF and adaptive throttling? I'll prepare incident channel comms and page owners.

Ben SRE: applying WAF denylist now and enabling a UA-based soft block rule. Commands:

```
wafctl rule add --name tmp-abuse-175900 --ips 45.77.96.0/22,103.21.50.0/24 --action block --ttl 90m
redwoodctl throttles set --route /v1/chat/completions --mode adaptive --suspicious-ua-pattern "python-requests|curl/7" --base 30/s
```

deploy-bot: WAF rule tmp-abuse-175900 deployed (id: w-1f2e). Edge propagation ~22s.

Ben SRE: also pushing a traffic-shaper lambda to short-circuit highly repetitive payloads (identical prompt hash) — drops and returns 429 with detailed Retry-After. Canary at 10%.

Devon Eng: canary up — sampling shows 48% of sampled requests dropped. No impact to enterprise keys in the canary sample.

Sasha Support: notifying affected customers now with ETA for mitigation. Message: "We're actively mitigating automated traffic; you may experience throttling briefly. Contact support to whitelist critical keys."

Carla PM: let's whitelist verified enterprise projects to avoid disruption. Which accounts are impacted?

Ben SRE: impacted projects: proj-33X, proj-77B. I can apply scoped bypass for those IDs only.

Gaurav-Sec: whitelist only with audit log and TTL. Also start an auth log hunt for credential stuffing indicators (many bad-password attempts, token reuse across IPs).

Ben SRE: applied scoped bypass for proj-33X and proj-77B. Commands executed:

```
redwoodctl project update --id proj-33X --bypass-waf true --ttl 2h
redwoodctl project update --id proj-77B --bypass-waf true --ttl 2h
```

Alice (oncall): sampling blocked requests for false positives. So far ~90% look automated (repeated payloads, same IP ranges, short intervals). Good signal.

Gaurav-Sec: auth hunt results — 720 failed token attempts over 30m from the denylist CIDRs; multiple token IDs reused across IP rotations. Probable credential stuffing. Recommend immediate rotation for tokens with suspicious activity and forcing password reset where applicable.

Carla PM: that may impact customers. Coordinate with Sasha to notify and provide expedited whitelist after rotation if needed.

Sasha Support: doing outreach to affected accounts. For any customer that needs continuity, we'll provide a temporary scoped token and assist with rotation.

Ben SRE: reduced public-tier QPS to 40/min and tightened burst to 8 for /v1/chat/completions to blunt scraping while enterprise stays higher. Added throttling headers to responses.

Alice (oncall): what's the rollback policy if we see legitimate impact?

Ben SRE: plan: keep WAF + shaper for 90m, monitor legitimate 429s, and relax per-key limits gradually. If customers complain, we'll whitelist per-project and document in incident. Rollback steps scripted.

Devon Eng: implementing an emergency bypass endpoint for on-call to whitelist a project id without a deploy — logs audited. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: emergency bypass endpoint deployed to control plane.

Ben SRE: metrics after mitigations: total RPS down 65% on offending ranges, 5xx steady at 0.6% (from 4.2%), median P50 latency improved 120ms. Cost anomaly reduced.

Gaurav-Sec: creating security incident INC-2026-1759001234 with tags [abuse, credential-stuffing, waf]. I'll follow up with forensics and IOCs for long-term blocks.

Carla PM: assigning postmortem to me. Need dashboards: auth-failures, blocked-ips list, customer-impact list, cost delta.

Sasha Support: escalations: proj-77B asked for immediate assistance — we rotated token and applied scoped whitelist; throughput restored.

Alice (oncall): handing off to Ben for ongoing monitoring. Ben acked.

Ben SRE: ack. I'll keep alerts tightened for next 2 hours and coordinate with Gaurav for follow-up.

Gaurav-Sec: next steps: 1) ingest IOCs into WAF/Edge 2) evaluate CAPTCHA / friction on suspicious flows 3) long-term: rate-limited login attempts and anomaly detection at auth layer.

Carla PM: action items logged. Thanks everyone — will publish postmortem and remediation plan later today. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: created persistent incident channel #incident-1759001234 and attached runbook. End of thread.
